summary: Module 4 CONTEXT: The Five Things AI Always Gets Wrong -- phase shift to Senior Engineer review mode. MICRO-EXERCISE: found all five in the sample createInvitation function: SECURITY = SQL injection (teamId/email interpolated into SQL strings, no parameterized queries) + IDOR (no check that req.user is admin/member of the team -- any authenticated user can invite to any team); EDGE CASES = no email validation (empty/null/invalid/injection payload), no already-member or self-invite guard, no UUID validation on teamId; ERROR HANDLING = catch swallows real error with console.log, generic 'something went wrong', and email failure after DB insert leaves a dangling invitation with no rollback; NAMING = createInvitation does three jobs (validate+persist+email), SELECT * when only team.name is used, raw query output held as domain object, log line leaks system structure; TEST COVERAGE = one happy-path test, mock returns the same value for BOTH queries (does not even verify correct queries run), no tests for auth/validation/404/duplicate/injection/email-failure/error paths, asserts status(201) but never the body -- false confidence. APPLIED THE SAME LENS TO MY REAL TEAM CODE: SECURITY = clean -- SQLAlchemy parameterized queries (no injection possible), require_owner/require_owner_or_admin on every protected endpoint (no IDOR), verified live in M2; EDGE CASES = strong -- empirical probe: 300-char name -> 400, whitespace name -> 400 (str_strip_whitespace + min_length), negative team id -> 404, team id 0 -> 404, dup member -> 409, invalid role -> 400; ERROR HANDLING = solid -- HTTPException -> error_envelope by construction, IntegrityError rollback on duplicate add; NAMING = consistent verb-first, split router/service/schema; TEST COVERAGE = THE REAL GAP -- the team feature has ZERO committed automated tests (agent was instructed not to add them; only live probe scripts exist in progress/). UX/edge finding: role Literal is case-sensitive so 'ADMIN' returns a generic 400 'invalid request' rather than a role-specific message -- a client typo gets an unhelpful error. Verdict: the five-category lens confirms the structural prediction -- happy paths are AI-strength, coverage is where AI output fails; my review duty is to close the test gap (M4 FIX/verify work) and tighten the generic validation message.
evidence: All 5 categories found in sample with exact locations (SQL strings, IDOR, no email validation, swallowed error, mock-reuse test)
Real code probe: m4_edge_probe.py 7 cases (unicode-ish 201, 300-char name 400, negative id 404, id 0 404, whitespace 400, ADMIN 400, dup 201)
Real code: SQLAlchemy parameterized, require_owner/owner_or_admin on all 5 endpoints, IntegrityError rollback
Real gap: no committed tests for team feature; generic 400 on role case typo
